text: Work out what the single byte 11001000 denotes under three different agreements. Give each fill as a plain number, except the last, which is two hex digits.
choices: (a) read as an unsigned binary numeral, 128+64+8 = ___
(b) read as two's complement: the leading 1 means negative, so the value is (a) - 256 = ___
(c) read as hexadecimal, grouping into 1100 and 1000 = 0x___
explanation: Verified: 200, -56, and 0xC8. Three answers, one pattern, and nothing in the bits chooses between them — which is the chapter's entire claim made arithmetic. The same eight wires, held at the same voltages, are a pixel's blue channel, a small negative number, and a byte of a UTF-8 sequence, depending only on which agreement the reader is operating under.
